mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW 6 Series 630d engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BMW 6 Series 630d engine replacement typically costs £2,300-£3,800 for a used N57 or B57 unit, £3,200-£4,600 for a reconditioned engine, and £4,200-£5,800 for a fully rebuilt engine with 12-month warranty. Supply and fit costs add approximately £800-£1,200 depending on your location and the specialist's labour rates.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of N57 or B57 engine failure in a BMW 6 Series 630d?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common signs of N57 or B57 engine trouble in a 630d include: rattling noise from the engine bay at startup (timing chain stretch), loss of power and warning lights (DPF/EGR blockage), excessive smoke from the exhaust (turbocharger failure), and rough idling or reduced performance.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a BMW 6 Series 630d?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes - if your BMW 6 Series 630d is otherwise in good condition, a replacement engine can extend its life by 80,000+ miles and retain strong value. With a typical 2014-2017 630d valued at £10,000-£18,000, a rebuilt engine at £4,200-£5,300 plus fitting represents a sound investment compared to the £7,500-£10,000 main dealer alternative.

mainEntity.name: How long does a BMW 6 Series 630d engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most BMW 6 Series 630d engine replacements take 1-3 days for supply and fit at a specialist garage. Collection and delivery options are available nationwide, with most engines dispatched within 24-72 hours of order confirmation.

mainEntity.name: Do BMW 6 Series 630d replacement engines come with a warranty?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes - all rebuilt BMW 6 Series 630d engines supplied through EnginesMarket include a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty. Used engines typically come with a 3-6 month warranty depending on the supplier, and reconditioned engines often carry a 12-24 month warranty.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the N57 and B57 engines in the BMW 6 Series 630d?

acceptedAnswer.text: The N57 (2008-2018) is BMW's previous-generation 3.0-litre diesel, available in single, twin and triple-turbo variants. The B57 (2015-present) is BMW's modular replacement, featuring a lightweight aluminum block, advanced common-rail injection, and improved emissions technology. B57 engines are generally more reliable and fuel-efficient, but both share common diesel-related issues like DPF and EGR clogging.

historyTimeline.h2: BMW 6 Series 630d - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The BMW 630d joined the 6 Series range as a 3.0-litre diesel option across two distinct generations: the E63 (2004-2010) and the F06/F12/F13 (2011-2018), before reappearing in the G32 Gran Turismo (2017-2023). The 630d nameplate has been powered by three generations of BMW's straight-six diesel engines - the M57, N57 and B57 families - making it one of the most technically diverse diesel badges in the 6 Series line-up.

milestones.description: M57D30, 3.0L turbocharged straight-six diesel, 231hp, launched with E63 Coupé and E64 Convertible
M57D30 (updated), 3.0L diesel, 235hp, facelift E63/E64 models with revised emissions
N57D30A, 3.0L twin-turbo straight-six diesel, 245hp, launched with F12 Convertible and F13 Coupé
N57D30A, F06 Gran Coupé joins the range
Facelift (LCI) updates across F06/F12/F13; N57D30B and N57D30C codes introduced with Euro 6 emissions compliance
B57D30O0, 3.0L single-turbo straight-six diesel, 261hp, launched with G32 Gran Turismo (5-door liftback)
B57D30A (265hp) and B57D30B mild-hybrid (286hp) variants introduced across G32 range
G32 production ends; 630d nameplate retired from UK 6 Series range

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the BMW 6 Series 630d is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: BMW 6 Series 630d Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The BMW 6 Series 630d has been powered by three generations of BMW's 3.0-litre straight-six diesel - the M57, N57 and B57. Replacement demand for the 630d is dominated by the N57D30 (2011-2018) and B57D30 (2017-2023) variants, with timing chain failure, DPF/EGR clogging, and turbocharger issues being the most frequent drivers of replacement decisions. Rebuilt BMW 6 Series 630d engines supplied through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Failure - Why the BMW 6 Series 630d N57 Engine Suffers Prematurely
problems.rootCause: Timing chain issues in N57 engines are often due to tensioner wear and chain stretch over time. Symptoms include rattling noise from the engine at startup, rough idle, and reduced performance. If the chain fails, valves collide with pistons, causing catastrophic engine damage.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing chain, tensioners, and guides
repairOptions.longevity: Suitable if caught early before catastrophic failure

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded timing chain components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended if chain failure has caused valve/piston damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2012-2015 BMW 6 Series 630d is valued between £8,000 and £18,000 depending on body style, mileage and condition. For vehicles worth £10,000-£15,000, a rebuilt engine at £4,200-£5,300 plus fitting is financially viable. For cars at the lower end of the value spectrum (under £8,000), a used or reconditioned engine may be the more sensible choice.
problems.recommendation: If you hear rattling from the engine bay at startup, have the timing chain inspected immediately. Early intervention with a chain and tensioner replacement (£1,500-£2,200 at a specialist) can prevent catastrophic engine failure. If the chain has already failed and damaged the engine, a rebuilt unit is the only sensible path forward.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt N57D30 BMW 6 Series 630d engine prices

problems.h4: DPF and EGR System Clogging - Why the BMW 6 Series 630d Diesel Suffers
problems.rootCause: Diesel Particulate Filter (DPF) blockage occurs when the vehicle is frequently driven on short trips that do not allow the engine to reach the temperatures needed for DPF regeneration. The Exhaust Gas Recirculation (EGR) valve becomes clogged with soot and carbon deposits over time. Symptoms include loss of power, poor fuel economy, warning lights, and failed MOT emissions tests.

repairOptions.longevity: Suitable if DPF is partially blocked

problems.vehicleValueCheck: For a 2017-2020 BMW 6 Series 630d G32 valued at £15,000-£25,000, DPF/EGR repairs are a worthwhile investment. Regular long drives at highway speeds can help prevent DPF blockages by allowing the filter to regenerate.
problems.recommendation: If your 630d's DPF or EGR system is causing issues, start with a forced regeneration or professional cleaning (£100-£800 at a specialist). If the vehicle has high mileage (80,000+) and the DPF and EGR are both heavily clogged, a full rebuilt engine with cleaned systems may offer better long-term value than piecemeal repairs.

problems.h4: Turbocharger Failure - Why the BMW 6 Series 630d Suffers
problems.rootCause: Turbocharger wear and failure is a common issue on high-mileage diesel engines. Symptoms include loss of power, excessive smoke from the exhaust, a whining noise from the engine bay, and increased fuel consumption. Regular maintenance, including timely oil changes, can help prolong turbocharger life.

A specialist rebuild (£900-£1,500) is significantly cheaper than a full engine replacement. However, if the turbo has failed catastrophically and sent debris through the engine, a full rebuilt unit is the only safe option.
